To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrochemical stability of SAMs prepared on Au(111)/Au(100) depends on the chemical nature of thiols/selenols (ATs vs ArTs) and on the crystalline plane of gold.
the Au(100) plane is more favorable to the formation of stable SAMs of aliphatic thiols, and that SAMs based on aromatic thiols are more stable on Au(111).
the Au(100) surface is more favorable for the adsorption of ATs and selenols than Au(111) due to the higher stability and the lower energy required to break the Au-S and Au-Se bonds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the crystalline plane and the nature of the adsorbate (thiol vs selenol) on the adsorption and the stability of the SAMs on Au surfaces.
the study of the adsorption of thiols and seltols on Au(hkl) surfaces.
the adsorption and self-assembly of thiols on gold single-crystal surfaces, and with the electrochemical properties of the resulting self-assembled monolayer (SAM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adsorption and the structure of the SAMs on gold are dependent on the crystallinity of the surface and the nature of the adsorbate.

the adsorption and the structural arrangements of SAMs prepared using aliphatic and aromatic thiols and selaenols on Au(100), and Au(111) are dependent on the chemical nature of both the thiol/selenol and the crystalline face of gold.
the Au crystalline face plays a role in the SAM stability and the Au-S/ Au-Se bond strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemical nature of both the adsorbate and the adsorbent are the key elements to understand the adsorption process of thiols and selsenols on gold.
the chemical nature of both the adsorbates and the surface plane play an important role in the adsorption process.
the Au(111)-S bond is more stable than the Au(100)-S bond.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Au(100) surface is a better candidate for the preparation of stable SAMs than Au(111).
the Au(hkl) surface plane plays a significant role in the adsorption of thiols and seltens on gold, which is not taken into account when comparing different SAMs prepared on gold.
the Au crystalline face plays a key role in the adsorption of thiolates and selenolates on gold surfaces, which is of great importance in the field of surface chemistry.
